summary: Steel 1931 lookout on Shoestring Butte, Fremont National Forest, Oregon; towers sold for scrap in 1968 and reported gone; no source describes the summit today.

facts.design: Steel Aermotor tower with a 7x7 cab and a one-room 12x16 living quarters
facts.status_note: Towers sold for scrap by October 1968 but not yet removed then; register says gone by 1968; no removal date in either source
facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service, Fremont National Forest

Shoestring and Slide Mountain towers sold for scrap; not yet removed as of October 23, 1968
Register says tower and cabin gone by 1968; no removal date given in either source
Registered June 10, 2011, nominated by Ray Kresek

corrections.why: The register's detail page gives N 42.386340 W 120.532860. The 1948 survey description places the summit about 17 miles northwest of Lakeview, which fits the register point; the brief point lies roughly 55 miles from Lakeview.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Register says 100 ft, a September 1931 entry says seventy-five feet, and the 1959 inspection report says 73 ft. The story and facts use 73 ft, the figure from the formal inspection report.
Register says gone by 1968; the October 1968 memo says the towers had been sold for scrap but not yet removed. The story reports both and gives no removal date, since neither source supplies one.

notes_for_editor: Only two sources. The Oregon page is a volunteer compilation that quotes Forest Service memos, a 1948 NGS station description and a Lake County Examiner item, and I did not check the originals. Brief coordinates disagree with the register by roughly 0.2 degrees latitude and 0.7 degrees longitude. Nothing found describes the summit today, so the story says so. The 1931 Cox Creek entry is quoted from the page's 1931 section, and the May 21, 1931 item is attributed to the Lake County Examiner as the page attributes it. Fact-check 2026-10-10: every quote found on the first run; story rewritten to match the page's wording and attributions.
